American Indian English.subject: Indian Languages
American Indian English.question: The _____ was Dialects of the English Language spoken by Native Americans.
American Indian English.fact: American Indian English or Native American English is a diverse collection of English dialects spoken by many American Indians and Alaska Natives, notwithstanding indigenous languages also spoken in the United States, of which only a few remain in daily use in the 21st century. For the sake of comparison, this article focuses on similarities across varieties of American Indian English that unite it in contrast to a "typical" English variety with standard grammar and a General American accent.

American Indian English.subject: Indian Languages
American Indian English.question: For example, _____ may have KIT–DRESS, KIT–FLEECE, or FACE–DRESS mergers, particularly word-medially
American Indian English.fact: For example, Navajo English may have KIT–DRESS, KIT–FLEECE, or FACE–DRESS mergers, particularly word-medially. Cheyenne and Navajo English, among others, follow General American patterns of glottal replacement of t, plus both t- and d-glottalization at the ends of syllables.

Amesha Spenta.subject: Indian Languages
Amesha Spenta.question: The _____ was Class of divine entities in Zoroastrianism.
Amesha Spenta.fact: In Zoroastrianism, the Amesha Spenta (Avestan: 𐬀𐬨𐬆𐬱𐬀⸱ 𐬯𐬞𐬆𐬧𐬙𐬀, romanized: Aməša Spəṇta—literally "Immortal (which is) holy/bounteous/furthering") are a class of seven divine entities emanating from Ahura Mazda, the highest divinity of the religion.

Amesha Spenta.subject: Indian Languages
Amesha Spenta.question: Like all other verses of the _____, Yasna 39.3 is also in Gathic Avestan and is approximately as old as the hymns attributed to Zoroaster himself
Amesha Spenta.fact: Spenta is a characteristic word of his revelation, meaning furthering, strengthening, bounteous, holy." The oldest attested use of the term is in part of the Yasna Haptanghaiti and in which the two elements of the name occur in reverse order, that is, as Spenta Amesha. Like all other verses of the Yasna Haptanghaiti, Yasna 39.3 is also in Gathic Avestan and is approximately as old as the hymns attributed to Zoroaster himself.

Amesha Spenta.fact: In the Gathas, each Amesha Spenta represents a good moral quality that mortals should strive to obtain. Anglo-Iraqi War.question: At this point in the _____, the situation developing in Iraq did not figure highly in British priorities

Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The Government of India had a long-standing commitment to prepare an infantry division to protect the Anglo-Iranian oilfields, and in July _____ the leading brigade of the 5th Indian Infantry Division
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The Government of India had a long-standing commitment to prepare an infantry division to protect the Anglo-Iranian oilfields, and in July 1940 the leading brigade of the 5th Indian Infantry Division was ordered to Iraq.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: In August, the division was placed under the control of _____ and diverted to the Sudan
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: In August, the division was placed under the control of Middle East Command and diverted to the Sudan.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Since then, GHQ India had been investigating the move of troops by air from India to RAF _____
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Since then, GHQ India had been investigating the move of troops by air from India to RAF Shaibah. The response from India was that most of a brigade group due to set sail for Malaya on 10 April, could be diverted to Basra and the rest sent ten days later; 390 British infantry could be flown from India into RAF Shaibah, and when shipping was available the force could quickly be built up to a division.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Amery contacted _____ and Lord Linlithgow, Viceroy and Governor-General of India, the same day
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Amery contacted General Auchinleck and Lord Linlithgow, Viceroy and Governor-General of India, the same day.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On 10 April this offer was accepted by _____, and the move of these forces was codenamed
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On 10 April this offer was accepted by London, and the move of these forces was codenamed. On the same day General Archibald Wavell, Commander-in-Chief of Middle East Command, informed London that he could no longer spare the battalion in Palestine and urged diplomacy and possibly a demonstration of air strength, rather than military intervention.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The attitude of the _____ and local authorities was still uncertain and attempts might be made to oppose disembarkation
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The attitude of the Iraqi Army and local authorities was still uncertain and attempts might be made to oppose disembarkation.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: If the landing was opposed, _____ was to defeat the Iraqi forces and establish a base, but Fraser was not to infringe Iranian neutrality
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On 10 April, Major-General William Fraser assumed control over Iraqforce, the land forces from India headed for Basra with orders to occupy the Basra-Shaibah area to ensure the safe disembarkation of further reinforcements and to enable a base to be set up in that area. Fraser was closely to co-operate with the navy commander.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: In early April, preparation for hostilities began at _____: aircraft were modified to carry bombs, and light bombers such as the Audaxes were modified to carry larger bombs
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: In early April, preparation for hostilities began at Habbaniya: aircraft were modified to carry bombs, and light bombers such as the Audaxes were modified to carry larger bombs.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages

Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On 12 April, Convoy BP7 left Karachi.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The convoy was composed of eight transports escorted by the _____-class sloop HMAS Yarra
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The convoy was composed of eight transports escorted by the Grimsby-class sloop HMAS Yarra.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The forces transported by the convoy were under the command of Major-_____, the commanding officer of the 10th Indian Infantry Division
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The forces transported by the convoy were under the command of Major-General Fraser, the commanding officer of the 10th Indian Infantry Division.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On 13 April, the _____ force of four ships in the Persian Gulf was reinforced by the aircraft carrier HMS Hermes and two light cruisers, HMS Emerald and HMNZS Leander
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On 13 April, the Royal Navy force of four ships in the Persian Gulf was reinforced by the aircraft carrier HMS Hermes and two light cruisers, HMS Emerald and HMNZS Leander.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: HMS Hermes carried the _____ torpedo bombers of 814 Squadron
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: HMS Hermes carried the Fairey Swordfish torpedo bombers of 814 Squadron.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On the morning of 15 April, _____ BP7 was met at sea by HMS Seabelle from Basra
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On the morning of 15 April, Convoy BP7 was met at sea by HMS Seabelle from Basra. On 17 April, the convoy was joined by HMIS Lawrence and then proceeded towards the entrance of the Shatt al-Arab.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On 18 _____, the convoy moved up the Shatt al-Arab and arrived at Basra at 0930 hrs
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On the morning of 15 April, Convoy BP7 was met at sea by HMS Seabelle from Basra. On 17 April, the convoy was joined by HMIS Lawrence and then proceeded towards the entrance of the Shatt al-Arab.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Later in the day the escort was reinforced by _____
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The naval vessels which covered the disembarkation at Basra consisted of the aircraft carrier HMS Hermes, the light cruiser HMS Emerald, the light cruiser HMNZS Leander, the sloop HMS Falmouth, the gunboat HMS Cockchafer, the sloop HMS Seabelle, the minesweeper sloop HMIS Lawrence, and the sloop HMAS Yarra. Later in the day the escort was reinforced by HMS Falmouth.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On 17 April, the convoy was joined by _____ and then proceeded towards the entrance of the Shatt al-Arab
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The naval vessels which covered the disembarkation at Basra consisted of the aircraft carrier HMS Hermes, the light cruiser HMS Emerald, the light cruiser HMNZS Leander, the sloop HMS Falmouth, the gunboat HMS Cockchafer, the sloop HMS Seabelle, the minesweeper sloop HMIS Lawrence, and the sloop HMAS Yarra. On 17 April, the convoy was joined by HMIS Lawrence and then proceeded towards the entrance of the Shatt al-Arab.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: HMS _____ was already in Basra
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: HMS Emerald was already in Basra.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On the same day, HMNZS _____ was released from support duties in the Persian Gulf
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On the same day, HMNZS Leander was released from support duties in the Persian Gulf.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On 16 April, the _____ was informed that the British were going to invoke the Anglo-Iraq treaty to move troops through the country to Palestine
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On 16 April, the Iraqi Government was informed that the British were going to invoke the Anglo-Iraq treaty to move troops through the country to Palestine.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Colonel Ouvry Roberts, the _____ of the 10th Indian Infantry Division, arrived with the 1st KORR
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Colonel Ouvry Roberts, the Chief Staff Officer of the 10th Indian Infantry Division, arrived with the 1st KORR.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: By 18 April, the airlift of the 1st KORR to _____ was completed
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: By 18 April, the airlift of the 1st KORR to Shaibah was completed.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The troop-carrying aircraft used for this airlift were 7 _____ and 4 Atalantas supplemented by 4 DC-2s which had recently arrived in India
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The troop-carrying aircraft used for this airlift were 7 Valentias and 4 Atalantas supplemented by 4 DC-2s which had recently arrived in India.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On 18 April, the 20th _____ landed at Basra, commanded by Brigadier Donald Powell
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On 18 April, the 20th Indian Infantry Brigade landed at Basra, commanded by Brigadier Donald Powell. The 20th Indian Infantry Brigade included the 2nd battalion 8th Gurkha Rifles, 2nd battalion 7th Gurkha Rifles, and the 3rd battalion 11th Sikh Regiment.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The 20th _____ included the 2nd battalion 8th Gurkha Rifles, 2nd battalion 7th Gurkha Rifles, and the 3rd battalion 11th Sikh Regiment
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The forces being transported consisted of two senior staff officers from the 10th Indian Division headquarters, the 20th Indian Infantry Brigade, the personnel of the Royal Artillery's 3rd Field Regiment—without their guns—and certain ancillary troops.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The landing of the force transported by _____7 was covered by infantry of the 1st KORR which had arrived the previous day by air
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The landing of the force transported by Convoy BP7 was covered by infantry of the 1st KORR which had arrived the previous day by air. By 19 April, the disembarkation of the force transported by Convoy BP7 at Basra was completed.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: By 19 April, the disembarkation of the force transported by _____7 at Basra was completed
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The landing of the force transported by Convoy BP7 was covered by infantry of the 1st KORR which had arrived the previous day by air. By 19 April, the disembarkation of the force transported by Convoy BP7 at Basra was completed.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On the same day, seven aircraft were flown into RAF _____ to bolster the air force there

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Following the landing of the 20th _____, Rashid Ali requested that the brigade be moved quickly through the country and that no more troops should arrive until the previous force had left
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Following the landing of the 20th Indian Infantry Brigade, Rashid Ali requested that the brigade be moved quickly through the country and that no more troops should arrive until the previous force had left.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Sir Kinahan Cornwallis, the _____ to Iraq, referred the issue to London and London replied that they had no interest in moving the troops out of the country and wanted to establish them within Iraq
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Sir Kinahan Cornwallis, the British Ambassador to Iraq, referred the issue to London and London replied that they had no interest in moving the troops out of the country and wanted to establish them within Iraq.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Sir Kinahan Cornwallis, the _____ located at the British Embassy in Baghdad and in contact with RAF Habbaniya via wireless, fully supported this action
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Sir Kinahan Cornwallis, the British Ambassador to Iraq, referred the issue to London and London replied that they had no interest in moving the troops out of the country and wanted to establish them within Iraq.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages

Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Cornwallis was directed not to make agreements with an Iraqi government which had usurped its power. In addition, he was directed to avoid entangling himself with explanations to the Iraqis.

Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Reconnaissance aircraft were launched before dawn from RAF _____, and reported that at least two battalions, with artillery, had taken up position on the plateau

Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The envoy also informed _____ that all flying should cease immediately and demanded that no movements, either ground or air, take place from the base
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The envoy also informed Smart that all flying should cease immediately and demanded that no movements, either ground or air, take place from the base. Smart replied that any interference with the normal training carried out at the base would be treated as an act of war.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: At 11:30 hours, the Iraqi envoy again made contact with Smart and accused the _____ of violating the Anglo-Iraqi treaty
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Sir Kinahan Cornwallis, the British Ambassador located at the British Embassy in Baghdad and in contact with RAF Habbaniya via wireless, fully supported this action. British reconnaissance aircraft, already in the air, continued to relay information to the base; they reported that the Iraqi positions on the plateau were being steadily reinforced and that Iraqi troops had occupied the town of Fallujah.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Smart replied that this was a political matter and he would have to refer the accusation to _____
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Sir Kinahan Cornwallis, the British Ambassador located at the British Embassy in Baghdad and in contact with RAF Habbaniya via wireless, fully supported this action. Smart replied that this was a political matter and he would have to refer the accusation to Cornwallis.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Meanwhile, Iraqi forces had now occupied vital bridges over the Tigris and _____ rivers and reinforced their garrison at Ramadi, cutting off land links to RAF Habbaniya
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Meanwhile, Iraqi forces had now occupied vital bridges over the Tigris and Euphrates rivers and reinforced their garrison at Ramadi, cutting off land links to RAF Habbaniya.

Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The 2,500 men included air crew and _____, who were prized by the British for their loyalty, discipline and fighting qualities

Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: The British Ambassador signalled the Foreign Office that he regarded the Iraqi actions as an act of war, which required an immediate air response.

Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Initially, the Iraqi siege of _____ and the ability of the besieged British force there to withstand the siege was the primary focus of the conflict
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Starting early on 2 May, British airstrikes were launched against the Iraqis from RAF Habbaniya. Initially, the Iraqi siege of RAF Habbaniya and the ability of the besieged British force there to withstand the siege was the primary focus of the conflict.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: While the relief force from _____ arrived in Habbaniya after the siege was over, it did allow an immediate change over to the offensive
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: While the relief force from Palestine arrived in Habbaniya after the siege was over, it did allow an immediate change over to the offensive.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: At 05:00 on 2 May 33 aircraft from _____, out of the 56 operational aircraft based there, and eight Wellington bombers from Shaibah began their attack

While the relief force from Palestine arrived in Habbaniya after the siege was over, it did allow an immediate change over to the offensive.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: A few of the Greek pilots being trained at _____ also joined in the RAF attack
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: While the relief force from Palestine arrived in Habbaniya after the siege was over, it did allow an immediate change over to the offensive. At 05:00 on 2 May 33 aircraft from Habbaniya, out of the 56 operational aircraft based there, and eight Wellington bombers from Shaibah began their attack.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Within minutes the _____ on the escarpment replied by shelling the base, damaging some planes on the ground
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Within minutes the Iraqis on the escarpment replied by shelling the base, damaging some planes on the ground.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: The Royal Iraqi Air Force (RIAF) also joined in the fray over _____
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: At 05:00 on 2 May 33 aircraft from Habbaniya, out of the 56 operational aircraft based there, and eight Wellington bombers from Shaibah began their attack. A few of the Greek pilots being trained at Habbaniya also joined in the RAF attack.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: By the end of the day, the Iraqi force outside _____ had grown to roughly a brigade
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Throughout the day, the pilots from Habbaniya flew 193 sorties and claimed direct hits on Iraqi transports, armoured cars and artillery pieces; however five aircraft had been destroyed and several others put out of service. By the end of the day, the Iraqi force outside Habbaniya had grown to roughly a brigade.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: While the _____ on the escarpment carried live ammunition, many Iraqi soldiers were under the impression that they were on a training exercise
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: While the Iraqis on the escarpment carried live ammunition, many Iraqi soldiers were under the impression that they were on a training exercise.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
Anglo-Iraqi War.question: Rashid Ali and the members of the _____ were shocked by the British defenders at RAF Habbaniya being prepared to fight rather than surrender
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: Rashid Ali and the members of the Golden Square were shocked by the British defenders at RAF Habbaniya being prepared to fight rather than surrender.

Anglo-Iraqi War.question: On 3 May, the _____ bombing of the Iraqis continued; troop and gun positions on the plateau were targeted as well as the supply line to Baghdad
Anglo-Iraqi War.fact: On 3 May, the British bombing of the Iraqis continued; troop and gun positions on the plateau were targeted as well as the supply line to Baghdad.

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages

Anglo-Iraqi War.subject: Indian Languages
